steps.title: The first mini recital
steps.body:
A recital is a piece played for people, start to finish, with its name said out loud first. Nothing else changes: the same piece, the same hands, one audience.

This week there is no new trick. You play two pieces for the family: the piece from these three weeks and one old piece you already knew.

1. Choose the two pieces. Write their names on a card.
2. Run each piece once a day, hard bars first, the way you practised.
3. On recital day, set the phone where it sees your hands, say each piece's name, and play.
4. Keep going through a slip. Nobody remembers a slip; everyone remembers a stop.
5. Bow at the end. The family asks one question about the piece.

Then write the Practice log about how it went.

figure.alt: Two boxes stacked, one for each of the two pieces on the recital card, run once a day, hard bars first, before recital day.

steps.title: Recital checklist
steps.body: Tick each one before recital day.
checklist: Two pieces chosen and their names written on a card
Each piece run once a day, hard bars first
Phone set where it sees the hands; a test clip checked for sound
Names said out loud before each piece, a bow at the end
The family asked one question, and you answered it

steps.title: Record the recital
steps.prompt: Record both pieces in one take, names said out loud, phone where it sees the hands. Slips stay in.
